chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah has made for the woman that she should endure the patience of ten men; so when she attains [her desire], He increases her strength [of desire] to that of ten men.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between women's and men's patience and desire according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the metaphysical balance between women's patience (sabr) and their sexual desire (shahwa), noting that their endurance is naturally equivalent to ten men. The text further implies that when desire is actualized, it adds an additional strength equal to ten men, highlighting a unique physiological and spiritual dynamic in female nature. This serves as a key text in Shia jurisprudence and theology for understanding gender-specific attributes and the rationale behind certain legal distinctions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Caused for the woman that she would observe the patience of ten men. So when she is aroused, her strength (of desire) increases to that of ten men’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah has placed ten times more patience in women above men, but when grown (excited) she has the force (of desire) like ten men.’”
